summary: Round 1 (new modules). The construction is Benzécri's: FJ(B) is the printed subset of J(B) × (ℝⁿ⁺¹ − {O}) with the induced topology (étalé on jets); ℛ is exactly the orbit relation of g • (j, m) = (g ∘ j, i(g) m) with i = isoGUR = isoGU, the p. 236 isomorphism GS ≃* GU (i(ḡ) = |det g|^{-1/n} g); F(B) is the orbit quotient with the quotient topology; the cone charts [(jet_y e, m)] ↦ m map π⁻¹(e.source) onto the open cone s⁻¹(e.target) and change by i(g) ∈ GU. F(B) is Hausdorff / connected / has a proper ℝ₊*-action from T2Space B / ConnectedSpace B alone, with nothing smuggled. F on morphisms (pushJet, map) reads « φ∘j₂ = j₁ » as j₁ = j₂ ∘ φ, which the scan confirms is the only well-typed reading — but the SCOPE's justification (« as in J(V₂)∘f ») is backwards (minor 1). unitIso / counitIso are natural, unitMap is chart-independent (unitMap_eq), and coneEquivalence : ConeCat (n+1) ≌ ProjCat n is not vacuous (scratch: ProjCat (n+1) ∋ the model sphere S(n+1), ConeCat (n+2) ∋ its cone). The object classes are DEC-124's verbatim. The finding is proved and fair: exists_iso_coneObj_iff is « the essential image of F among Hausdorff connected cones is exactly the proper ones », EssSurjAsPrintedDim is a genuine necessary consequence of the printed Énoncé, refuted for every Benzécri n ≥ 3 and true for n ≤ 2 — but it rests entirely on plan F6 (B Hausdorff), since the counterexample IS isomorphic to F of its own non-Hausdorff base (scratch cexIso, one line), and two docstrings drop that qualifier (minor 2). Hygiene clean. Two minors (docstring/REPORT prose), three nits; no blocker, no major. Ready to graduate; the mark is the author's ruling, and the DEC-124 analogy holds.

fidelity_summary: The construction F(B) = FJ(B)/ℛ is Benzécri's, sentence by sentence: the printed subset and topology of FJ(B), the printed relation ℛ through the p. 236 isomorphism i : GS ≅ GU, the quotient topology, cone charts onto open cones with transitions in GU, and F(φ) through φ'(j₁, m) = (j₂, m) under the only well-typed reading of « φ∘j₂ = j₁ » (j₁ = j₂∘φ; the printed order is a slip, and the SCOPE's justification for it should be corrected). F(B) is genuinely Hausdorff, connected and proper from B Hausdorff and connected. Both natural isomorphisms are canonical and natural (unitMap chart-independent), and coneEquivalence : ConeCat (n+1) ≌ ProjCat n holds over DEC-124's object classes exactly, on inhabited categories. The finding is proved and fair: among Hausdorff connected cones the essential image of F is exactly the proper ones, so the printed Énoncé (F6 reading on both sides) fails for every Benzécri n ≥ 3 and holds for n ≤ 2 — with the qualification that the counterexample is F of its own non-Hausdorff base, so the failure is Prop. 2's (the base is not a « variété ») propagated, which two docstrings should say. Graduation: ready, conditional on the author's ruling on the mark; the two minors and the nits are docstring/REPORT edits (and one optional dead-line/structure cleanup) the master can make at curation without a re-audit of the mathematics.
graduation: ready, conditional on the author's ruling on the mark (question 1); minors 1–2 are docstring/REPORT prose and a proposed transcription [sic], the nits are optional cleanups
marking_assessment: By analogy with DEC-124 the label is eligible to be MARKED in corrected form, and nothing in the module blocks it: (i) DEC-113 already rules the reading « isomorphisme fonctoriel » = CategoryTheory.Equivalence; (ii) DEC-122 rules that wave 4's affine conical objects carry a proper ℝ₊* action and DEC-124 fixes both object classes, which ConeCat (n+1) / ProjCat n match verbatim; (iii) the printed form is refuted and kept as the paper finding (not_essSurjAsPrinted_dim, with its n ≤ 2 positive form essSurjAsPrinted_of_le_one), exactly the Prop. 2 / Déf. 3 pattern of DEC-124; (iv) 0 sorry, standard axioms. CAMPAIGN.md's « no added hypothesis » rule is overridden only by an explicit ruling, and DEC-124 marked Prop. 2 / Déf. 3 but did not name this Énoncé, so the author must say MARKED. Corrected statement of record (`Benzecri.coneEquivalence n`, Prop form `baseFunctor_isEquivalence`): « For every n ≥ 1 (Benzécri's n; Lean's n+1), the correspondence V ↦ V/ℝ₊* is an equivalence of categories from the connected, Hausdorff affine conical n-manifolds WHOSE ℝ₊*-ACTION IS PROPER (equivalently, whose base is Hausdorff) to the connected, Hausdorff locally projective (n−1)-manifolds, morphisms the (G,X)-morphisms on both sides; its inverse is F, B ↦ FJ(B)/ℛ, φ ↦ F(φ) induced by φ'(j₁, m) = (j₂, m) with j₁ = j₂ ∘ φ; the unit V ≅ F(V/ℝ₊*) is m ↦ [(p(jet_m f), f(m))] and the counit F(B)/ℝ₊* ≅ B is the source projection.
